A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LCPO research, with matching core formulations and retained experiments. The main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original grid-world, wind-driven Pendulum and straggler-mitigation experiments, plus action-space validation in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports original results across six evaluation environments, the grid-world illustration, and additional sensitivity and diagnostic experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: V2 retains v1's LCPO-S procedure as LCPO, but removes the doubly constrained LCPO-D and proximal LCPO-P alternatives. It adds bounded reservoir sampling to the accumulating experience archive described in v1. Automatic entropy regularization was already used in v1; its explicit inclusion in v2's objective is not a new component.

E1.justification: V2 adds wind-driven InvertedPendulum-v4, InvertedDoublePendulum-v4, Hopper-v4 and Reacher-v4 evaluations. These substantially broaden the control tasks beyond v1's Pendulum-v1 and straggler mitigation. The grid-world example, four synthetic wind traces and two real workloads are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with MBCD, MBPO and online EWC alongside the retained A2C, TRPO, DDQN, SAC and offline-oracle comparisons. Appendix A.2 also compares against Ideal MBPO using ground-truth dynamics. MBPO is additionally included in the wind-free Pendulum validation.

E3.justification: V2 introduces normalized-return aggregation, limited-buffer settings, buffer-size sweeps, EWC tuning protocols and a ground-truth-model MBPO control. It also revises the stated straggler OOD thresholds from -5/-6/-7 to 5/6/7, with corresponding interpretation changes. This reported correction does not establish that the underlying implementation changed.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of buffer-size sensitivity, EWC hyperparameter sensitivity, change-point detector sensitivity and whether model error explains MBPO's weakness. It removes v1's LCPO-S/D/P comparison while retaining the OOD-threshold sensitivity analysis. These changes substantially alter the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: The stated seed counts rise from five to ten for straggler mitigation and the wind-free Pendulum validation; the main wind-driven control experiments remain at five. V2 explicitly reports 95% confidence bounds or ranges and latency uncertainty bands, whereas v1's result tables provide point estimates without confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive MuJoCo and diagnostic results and revises retained-task estimates. For example, Pendulum trace 3 changes from LCPO-S -194 in v1 Table 1 to LCPO -237 in v2 Table 2; revised settings prevent interpreting this as a controlled performance decline. The new Reacher results show DDQN and online EWC outperforming LCPO on all four traces.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix A.1's dual/KKT derivation for the doubly constrained optimization problem, including Equations 5–12, is removed entirely. V2 retains the former LCPO-S trust-region formulation and explicitly states the existing policy-gradient and entropy objectives, but supplies no replacement derivation for the removed solver.

C1.justification: The central claims of combating forgetting without task labels and approaching offline-oracle performance remain. V2 drops the three-solver contribution, adds an explicit small-buffer effectiveness claim and extends its comparative claim to model-based methods.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of MBPO's sampling bias and online EWC's adaptation–retention tradeoff, plus limitations concerning network capacity and more complex contexts requiring larger buffers. V1's explanations for surpassing offline policies and LCPO-P's weaker performance disappear. The exploration limitation is retained and expanded.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code URL, hardware and runtime information, tuning procedures, OOD sampling details and new-baseline hyperparameters. Software documentation changes from OpenAI Gym 0.26.2 to Gymnasium 0.29.1 and MuJoCo 3.1.1. Some earlier straggler specifications, including the full observation and reward description, are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated latent-context literature discussion and substantially expands positioning within observed exogenous-context RL, citing works such as Zintgraf, Caccia, Chen, Feng and Sinclair. It also develops comparisons with model-based learning and online EWC. The LCPO-P relationship to editable neural networks and its Sinitsin citation disappear.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and replaces input terminology with context terminology throughout. It substantially rewrites the introduction and methodology, swaps Preliminaries and Related Work, reorganizes evaluation around comparisons and sensitivities, and adds separate Discussion and Limitations and Broader Impact sections. The appendices are also extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the grid-world illustration into two modes and combines its two performance plots. It adds change-point, normalized-return, EWC and buffer-size figures; removes the Pendulum learning-curve figure; relocates trace and systems illustrations to the appendices; and substantially expands result tables and uncertainty displays.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical coverage and limited diagnostic and uncertainty reporting. Additional control tasks, relevant baselines, memory and model-error controls, confidence ranges and reproducibility disclosures make the evidence much more informative. These gains outweigh the narrower solver coverage and some lost environment detail. The broad superiority wording nevertheless needs qualification given the Reacher exceptions in Table 2.
